samples.summary: The `command: commandPath(this)` wiring into the injected-IO orchestrators (docs/notes/slides import, files upload, files download) is never exercised — every test calls the `run*` functions directly and omits `command`, so dropping the wiring from any of the five actions would keep the suite green
samples.evidence: `docs.ts:356`, `notes.ts:249`, `slides.ts:249`, `files.ts:46` and `files.ts:76` newly pass `command: commandPath(this)`. Every test that drives those orchestrators calls them directly without a `command` (packages/cli/test/upstream-error.test.ts:685-870 CASES all pass e.g. `{ file: 'a.docx', replace: 'doc-1', yes: true }`, and the assertions at 877/886 expect envelopes with **no** `command` field). The only attribution assertions in the new tests are on `errorEnvelope`/`upstreamErrorJson` in isolation (test/output.test.ts:354-372, 380-470) and on the throwing commands driven through commander (`docs.get`, `sheets.cells.get`, `docs.content`, `schema`, `ctx.switch`, runCli). Nothing asserts that e.g. `wafflebase files upload` actually emits `command: "files.upload"`.

samples.summary: Two of the rewritten cookie-policy tests assert only inside a `for` over `res.cookie`/`res.clearCookie` mock calls with no call-count assertion, so they pass vacuously if the cookie-setting path emits nothing at all
samples.evidence: `'sets SameSite=Lax with secure=false outside production'` (auth.controller.spec.ts:556-568) iterates `(res.cookie as jest.Mock).mock.calls` and asserts name/options, but unlike the production case (which asserts `toHaveBeenCalledTimes(2)` at :540) it never asserts any cookie was set. Same for `'never sets SameSite=None on auth cookies'` (:570-584), whose whole body is a loop over the combined `cookie`+`clearCookie` calls. If `controller.refresh` ever short-circuits (its mocks are hand-wired in `issueCookies`, e.g. a changed refresh-cookie name would make `req.cookies?.[refreshCookieName()]` miss and return early via `sendStatus`), both tests still pass while asserting nothing — the exact regression the rewrite was meant to pin.

samples.summary: The pino `req` serializer wiring — the only production caller of `logSafeUrl` — has no test; only the pure function is covered
samples.evidence: `log-safe-url.spec.ts` exercises `logSafeUrl` exhaustively, but nothing asserts that `app.module.ts`'s serializer applies it (or that `remoteAddress`/`userAgent`/`url` still come out as expected). Reverting `url: logSafeUrl(req.url)` to `url: req.url` would leave the whole backend suite green.
searchedFor: grep 'logSafeUrl|serializers' across packages/backend/src (only app.module.ts, log-safe-url.ts and its spec match)

samples.summary: `cliConfirmToken`'s parameter binding is tested for `port` and `challenge` but not for `nonce`, and the length-prefixing anti-ambiguity claim is untested
samples.evidence: The new replay tests cover a changed `port` (:161) and a changed `challenge` (:174). No test replays a confirmation against a *different nonce*, even though the middleware recomputes with `nonce` (cli-login-confirm.middleware.ts:149) and the doc comment (:94-95) specifically claims the length prefixes stop two different parameter tuples from signing the same — nothing exercises that collision case either.

samples.summary: `announceLoginUrl`'s TTY branch, its owner-only file mode, and its write-failure fallback are untested; only the non-TTY happy path is
samples.evidence: login-callback.test.ts asserts the non-TTY path (a notice naming `login-url.txt`, its contents, and its removal after the flow). Nothing covers `process.stderr.isTTY === true` (which prints the secret-bearing URL to the console), nothing asserts the `mode: 0o600` / prior-`rmSync` claim that the file is readable only by its owner, and nothing drives the `catch` branch that prints the 'could not open a browser' message.

samples.summary: `expect(CALLBACK_TIMEOUT_MS).toBe(5 * 60 * 1000)` restates the constant it imports; the 'two ends now expire together' claim about the backend's five-minute state TTL is not actually checked
samples.evidence: The comment says 'the two ends must agree' and cites the backend's `STATE_COOKIE_MAX_AGE_MS`/`CliAuthStore` entry, but the assertion compares the CLI constant against a hard-coded literal in the same file — it cannot fail if the backend TTL changes. The surrounding fake-timer assertions are meaningful; only this line is tautological.

Every test that drives those orchestrators calls them directly without a `command` (packages/cli/test/upstream-error.test.ts:685-870 CASES all pass e.g. `{ file: 'a.docx', replace: 'doc-1', yes: true }`, and the assertions at 877/886 expect envelopes with **no** `command` field). verdict.reason: The finding is accurate. docs.ts:356, notes.ts:249, slides.ts:249, files.ts:46 and files.ts:76 pass `command: commandPath(this)` into the injected-IO orchestrators, but nothing in the suite exercises that wiring. The import/upload/download cases in upstream-error.test.ts:685-870 call runDocsImport/runNotesImport/runSlidesImport/runFilesUpload/runFilesDownload directly with no `command`, and the assertions at 877-886 expect envelopes containing only `code`/`message` — they pass identically with the wiring removed. The one commander-driven attribution table (upstream-error.test.ts:267-341, which derives the expected dotted `command` from argv) omits import/upload/download entirely, covering only content/export/list/create/get/rename/delete, sheets *, files list|get|rename|delete and api-keys *. Repo-wide grep for the dotted names 'files.upload', 'files.download', 'notes.import', 'slides.import' yields zero test hits, and 'docs.import' only in the isolated errorEnvelope unit test (output.test.ts:356) and schema registry assertions. Every command-attribution assertion in the suite (output.test.ts:300,307,327,368,468,471,633; ctx.test.ts:140,166) is either a unit call to errorEnvelope/upstreamErrorJson or an outputError/forwardUpstreamError path (docs.get, docs.content, sheets.cells.get, schema, ctx.switch, runCli 'boom'). The per-orchestrator suites (files-upload.test.ts, files-download.test.ts, docs-import.test.ts, notes-import.test.ts, slides-import.test.ts) contain no occurrence of 'command' at all, and no structural/source-inspection test asserts the wiring. Blocking under the test-adequacy rubric: a behavior change (per-command error attribution for five commands) with no meaningful test covering it.

finding.summary: Two of the rewritten cookie-policy tests assert only inside a `for` over `res.cookie`/`res.clearCookie` mock calls with no call-count assertion, so they pass vacuously if the cookie-setting path emits nothing at all
finding.evidence: `'sets SameSite=Lax with secure=false outside production'` (auth.controller.spec.ts:556-568) iterates `(res.cookie as jest.Mock).mock.calls` and asserts name/options, but unlike the production case (which asserts `toHaveBeenCalledTimes(2)` at :540) it never asserts any cookie was set. Same for `'never sets SameSite=None on auth cookies'` (:570-584), whose whole body is a loop over the combined `cookie`+`clearCookie` calls. If `controller.refresh` ever short-circuits (its mocks are hand-wired in `issueCookies`, e.g. a changed refresh-cookie name would make `req.cookies?.[refreshCookieName()]` miss and return early via `sendStatus`), both tests still pass while asserting nothing — the exact regression the rewrite was meant to pin.

verdict.reason: The two tests are shaped as described (loops over `mock.calls` with no call-count assertion at spec:556-568 and :570-584), but the vacuous state they are claimed to hide is unreachable. The reviewer's named mechanism is factually wrong: the missing-refresh-token branch does not "return early via sendStatus" — auth.controller.ts:274-277 throws UnauthorizedException, and `issueCookies` awaits `controller.refresh` with no catch (spec:532), so that path makes the test FAIL, not pass vacuously. The request key is also derived from `refreshCookieName()` itself (spec:529), the same function the controller reads (controller.ts:266), so a rename cannot desynchronize them. The other exits are mocked to succeed (spec:516-523) and rethrow on failure (controller.ts:301-308); `fromBody` is false since the request has a cookie and no body (controller.ts:271, spec:528-530). The only residual way `res.cookie` could emit nothing — `setAuthCookies` no longer calling `res.cookie` — is pinned by the pre-existing sibling test asserting exact `res.cookie` calls (spec:104-113). For the second test the loop is unconditionally non-empty anyway, since `logout` → `clearAuthCookies` always emits six `clearCookie` calls (controller.ts:349-361). Under the current code both loops run two iterations and the inner assertions are falsifiable (they fail if secure flips to true in dev, if sameSite becomes 'none', or if names gain the `__Host-` prefix), so this is a missing-count style weakness, not fake coverage that can survive the gate.
